question.problem:
The rate at which customers enter a store one afternoon is given by the function

$$
r(t)=6{e}^{t}+3,
$$

where $r(t)$ is measured in customers per hour and $t>0$ is the time in hours since $1\,\text{p.m}.$
Customers are also leaving the store at a steady rate of $5$ customers per hour.

If there were $40$ customers in the store at $1\,\text{p.m},$ how many customers will be there at $4\,\text{p.m}?$

Rounded to the nearest integer, there will be 
{{field-1}}  customers in the store at $4\,\text{p.m}.$
question.worked_solution:
Customers are entering the store at a rate of $6{e}^{t}+3$ customers per hour and are leaving at a rate of $5$ customers per hour. Therefore, the **rate of change** in the number of customers (call it $R(t)$) is

$$
\begin{aligned}R(t) & =r(t)-5 \\  & =6{e}^{t}+3-5 \\  & =6{e}^{t}-2.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the **total number of customers** after $t$ hours (call it $T(t)$), we apply the second fundamental theorem of calculus:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =T(0)+{\int }_{0}^{t}R(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =40+{\int }_{0}^{t}(6{e}^{t}-2)\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

To ensure that $T$ is a function of $t$ only, we use a different variable ($x$) for the integration. 

To find out the number of packages after $3$ hours ($4\,\text{p.m}$), we substitute $t=3$ into the above and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(3) & =40+{\int }_{0}^{3}(6{e}^{t}-2)\,\text{d}x \\  & =40+(6{e}^{t}-2t){|}_{0}^{3} \\  & =40+[(6{e}^{3}-2(3))-(6{e}^{0}-2(0))] \\  & =40+6{e}^{3}-12 \\  & =6{e}^{3}+28 \\  & ≈149\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to the nearest integer. 

Therefore, there will be $149$ customers in the store at $4\,\text{p.m}.$
